title: Use the AI on this computer in {name}: private, free and offline
description: {name} can download a brain that runs on your own computer: nothing you write leaves it, it costs nothing and works offline. What your computer needs, and how.
h1: Use the AI on this computer
works: A computer with about 12 GB of memory, in a browser that lets a page use its graphics chip, Chrome or Edge for instance
answer: Where your computer can run one, {name} offers a brain of its own, under {free} in {settings} › {brains} › {add}: {device}. It downloads once, about 3 GB, and from then on nothing it answers leaves this computer. It’s free and works offline, with simpler, slower answers than the cloud’s.
tour.here: This is {settings} › {brains}, where brains are added. Next time, {settings} is in your menu at the foot of the task list.
tour.free: When this computer can run a brain itself, {device} is here, under {free}: open it. When it can’t, it isn’t offered.
need: A computer, not a phone or a tablet, with about 12 GB of memory or more.
A recent graphics chip that your browser lets a page use. Chrome and Edge do on most recent computers.
About 3.6 GB of free room, for a download of about 3 GB, once.
steps: Open {settings}, from your menu at the foot of the task list, then {brains}, and press {add}.
Under {free}, choose {device}. If it isn’t there, this computer can’t run one: see what it needs above.
Press its button to download it. You can keep using {name} meanwhile: until it’s ready, any other brain you have answers.
Once it’s ready, {name} says {ready}. From then on, {auto} answers with it anything personal, and everything while you’re offline.
To have every request answered here, choose {keep} under {who}, in {brains}.
good: The first time, {first} offers it beside OpenRouter, as {also}: it downloads while OpenRouter answers, and {auto} then has both.
Under an answer it wrote, {name} says {local}.
Each browser keeps its own download: in another browser on this computer, it downloads again.
If loading it ever closes the tab, this browser stops offering it and deletes the download, to free the room.
fixes: This computer lacks one of what it needs: the memory, a graphics chip the browser can use, or the room. Try Chrome or Edge, or free some room. Otherwise, a brain in the cloud answers instead: see {openrouter}.
The connection dropped, or the browser ran short of room. Press its button again.
It works on this computer’s own chip, which is slower than a service’s. With a brain in the cloud as well, {auto} keeps this one for what’s personal and gives the rest to the cloud: see {choose}.
ask: Can this computer run a brain of its own?
